stem: Which element is expected in a healthcare facility emergency action plan for fire or another workplace emergency?

options.A: Procedures for reporting an emergency, evacuation and exit-route assignments, accounting for personnel, and designated rescue or medical duties when applicable.
options.B: A plan to keep all personnel at their workstations until an external agency arrives, regardless of evacuation instructions or immediate hazards.
options.C: A requirement that only managers know the evacuation route so staff movement can be controlled during an emergency.
options.D: A policy to disable alarms during drills and emergencies so patients are not disturbed by warning signals.

rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 requires an emergency action plan to include, at minimum, procedures for reporting fires or other emergencies; emergency evacuation procedures and exit-route assignments; procedures for critical operations before evacuation when applicable; accounting for employees after evacuation; rescue and medical duties for designated employees; and contact information for plan questions. OSHA also requires an employee alarm system and training/review of the plan. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize core OSHA emergency-action-plan elements, including emergency reporting, evacuation/exit routes, personnel accountability, and assigned rescue or medical duties when applicable.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.38(c) Minimum elements of an emergency action plan; §1910.38(d) Employee alarm system; §1910.38(e)-(f) training/review requirements.
source_claim_supported: A workplace emergency action plan includes procedures for reporting emergencies, evacuation and exit routes, accounting for personnel, designated rescue/medical duties when applicable, alarm systems, and employee training/review.

source_original.stem: Which element is expected in a healthcare facility emergency action plan for fire or another workplace emergency?

options.A: Procedures for reporting the emergency, evacuation and exit-route assignments, accounting for personnel, and designated rescue or medical duties when applicable
options.B: A plan to keep all personnel at their workstations until an external agency arrives, regardless of evacuation instructions or immediate hazards
options.C: A requirement that only managers know the evacuation route so staff movement can be controlled during an emergency
options.D: A policy to disable alarms during drills and emergencies so patients are not disturbed by warning signals

source_original.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 requires emergency action plans to include procedures for reporting emergencies, evacuation and exit-route assignments, critical operations when applicable, accounting for employees after evacuation, designated rescue or medical duties, and plan contacts. An employee alarm system and plan training/review are also required.
source_original.source_detail: 29 CFR 1910.38(c) Minimum elements of an emergency action plan; 1910.38(d) employee alarm system; 1910.38(e)-(f) training/review requirements.

correction_summary: Retained key A and aligned it directly to OSHA's minimum emergency-action-plan elements; preserved alarms/training in the rationale and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct regulatory safety requirement.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item reproduces required EAP elements without inventing manager-only evacuation knowledge or disabling alarms.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because emergency plans include evacuation procedures rather than universal shelter-at-workstation until outside arrival.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because employees must be informed/trained on the emergency plan and evacuation procedures.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because OSHA requires an employee alarm system rather than disabling alarms.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A describes minimum EAP content required by OSHA.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are facility emergency-plan features and require regulatory safety knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — emergency response and environmental safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read OSHA §1910.38 and healthcare fire-safety materials, source snapshot, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
